description: Jurisdiction-specific rent-increase compliance rules for Canadian provinces. Percentages verified against ontario.ca and gov.bc.ca. Update annually (guidelines are announced ~Aug-Oct).

rentIncreaseGuidelines.source: ontario.ca — RTA s.120, guideline capped at 2.5%

rentIncreaseRules.notes: Guideline is capped at 2.5% even when inflation is higher. Units first occupied after November 15, 2018 are exempt from the guideline (rent control does not apply).

N1.name: Notice of Rent Increase
N1.description: Required 90-day written notice before increasing rent

N4.name: Notice to End Tenancy — Non-Payment of Rent
N4.description: 14-day notice when tenant has not paid rent

N11.name: Agreement to End the Tenancy
N11.description: Mutual agreement between landlord and tenant to end early

N12.name: Notice to End Tenancy — Landlord's Own Use
N12.description: 60-day notice when landlord needs the unit for personal use

L1.name: Application to Evict for Non-Payment of Rent
L1.description: Filed with the LTB after the N4 notice period expires

rentIncreaseRules.notes: Three full calendar months' written notice required. Increase can only occur once every 12 months.

RTB-7.description: Notice of rent increase (3 full calendar months)

RTB-7.name: Notice of Rent Increase
RTB-7.description: Three full calendar months' written notice before increasing rent

RTB-30.name: Notice to End Tenancy for Unpaid Rent
RTB-30.description: 10-day notice when tenant has not paid rent

RTB-8.name: Mutual Agreement to End Tenancy
RTB-8.description: Both landlord and tenant agree to end the tenancy early

RTB-32L.name: Notice to End Tenancy — Landlord Occupancy
RTB-32L.description: Notice when landlord needs the unit for personal use
